The project falls under the Regional Migration Governance Programme (RMGP) for the Mediterranean, funded by the Danish Foreign Affairs Ministry. 

The project runs from 1/12/2024 to 30/11/2029

projects.name: IOM plans to provide direct medical assistance, Health Assessment (resettlement), convoy assistance, mental health and psychosocial support assistance, health awareness and capacity building of community leaders.
projects.description: IOM will provide comprehensive health support to vulnerable migrants, refugees, and asylum seekers, with a particular focus on women and girls. Activities will include specialized healthcare assistance such as mental health and sexual and reproductive health services, direct medical care including primary healthcare, referrals to specialized services, surgical operations, rehabilitation, and life-saving interventions. Through medical convoys, health awareness sessions, and capacity building of community leaders, IOM aims to enhance community resilience and health knowledge. Additionally, IOM will conduct health assessments for refugees undergoing resettlement, ensuring that medical needs are addressed with culturally sensitive care, including screening, laboratory testing, vaccination, and referrals for ongoing treatment when necessary. Health education will be provided to empower migrants to manage their well-being and access healthcare services in their destination countries.

projects.name: Skills, knowledge, capacities and capabilities of government entities, youth-led organizations and networks, and local civil society organizations (CSOs) is enhanced to address negative social norms and promote women's empowerment
projects.description:
UNFPA-supported interventions strengthened the skills, knowledge, and institutional capacities of youth-led organizations and civil society partners to address negative social norms through structured, mandate-aligned capacity development and supported platforms for youth-led action. A total of 651 youth and young people were capacitated through partner-led mechanisms (472 through Etijah and 179 through Misr Foundation), with deliberate inclusion of 40 persons with disabilities, enhancing the readiness of youth cadres to act as facilitators, advocates, and community mobilizers.

Through Etijah, UNFPA strengthened the Population Awareness Clubs (PACs) delivery system by building the facilitation, leadership, and community engagement capacities of trained youth facilitators across governorates. Capacitated youth demonstrated improved competencies in participatory facilitation, edutainment-based engagement, and values-based dialogue on gender equality, reproductive health, family planning, the prevention of harmful practices, and violence against women and girls, supported by SOP-oriented trainings and refresher mechanisms to ensure quality and sustainability.

In parallel, implementation with Misr Foundation strategically strengthened youth capacities to address FGM medicalization by equipping youth—particularly within medical and advocacy cohorts—with evidence-based knowledge, ethical frameworks, and advocacy and communication skills to challenge harmful norms. Cinema- and arts-based methodologies were leveraged to support rights-based dialogue and youth-led norm change, including among youth with disabilities.

Complementing community-based capacity development, UNFPA strengthened youth psychosocial awareness and resilience as an enabling factor for sustained engagement on GBV prevention and social norm change. In partnership with Ministry of Youth and Sports and Etijah (national NGO), UNFPA supported 2,749 women and girls from refugee and host communities with livelihoods and vocational training. The sessions included various handicraft workshops such as sewing, hairdressing, and macrame and perfume-making.

projects.name: Sudanese Artists in Transit wil be supported to promote exchange with host community through arts and creativity
projects.description: Between 2024 and 2025, the UNESCO Regional Office for Egypt and Sudan implemented an integrated, gender-responsive crisis and recovery portfolio reaching at least 590 direct beneficiaries, while engaging several thousand more through public advocacy and digital outreach, to safeguard heritage and strengthen the livelihoods and skills of conflict-affected cultural communities. Core actions combined heritage risk mitigation—notably the April 2024 Cairo workshop with 70 heritage professionals from government, academia, and international partners that updated Sudan’s National Risk Register—with evidence-based, people-centred programming, including two comprehensive needs-mapping studies covering approximately 160 displaced Sudanese and Palestinian artists, complemented by a 60-person community consultation in Cairo. Strong emphasis was placed on skills development and professional empowerment, through policy dialogue and capacity-oriented platforms such as the International Migrant Day “Arts in Transit” celebration at AUC, which convened over 200 participants, showcased migrant artists’ work, and connected creators directly with policymakers around cultural rights and the Status of the Artist, while also amplifying voices to around 5,000 online viewers. The Office further strengthened local delivery ecosystems by convening 40 UNESCO, UN, and NGO partners in Port Sudan to form operational networks and develop joint proposals, and by advancing institutional sustainability through regional museum dialogues that contributed to the formal establishment of ICOM Sudan. Gender equality was embedded as a cross-cutting priority, most visibly through the “Stitch by Stitch” embroidery workshops, which empowered 60 Palestinian refugee and Egyptian women using Tatreez as a medium for psychosocial healing, heritage transmission, and practical digital skills training that supports creative income generation and economic resilience. Collectively, these actions demonstrate a coherent approach that links emergency response, gender-responsive design, and transferable skills training to reinforce cultural resilience, social inclusion, and sustainable recovery for displaced and host communities.

children.name: By 2027 women and girls realize their rights in social health and livelihood spheres as laid out in the Egyptian Constitution, and their leadership and empowerment are guaranteed in a society free of all forms of discrimination and violence against women and girls.
children.description: This is a cross-cutting outcome across all the other four outcomes

children.name: Output 5.1: Women’s civic engagement, leadership, decision-making and participation in public life is increased and there is improved understanding of the importance of women’s well-being, maternity as a social function, and their social, economic and political contributions

Output 5.2: Women have increased control over and access as well as retention to decent employment, economic opportunities and resources within an enabling environment supporting women’s engagement in the world of work to have safe working places.
Output 5.3: Women and girls’ exposure to risks of violence, and harmful practices, are reduced through scaled-up access to quality, coordinated prevention, response, care and protection services.

Output 5.4: Adolescent girl’s social, health and economic capacities are built and social support provided for strengthened capabilities and equal access to quality services and opportunities to reach their full potential.
